title: Parche — build sites you don't just fork
description: A minimal blog demo built with Parche: pages as data, rendered through a virtual-module registry.

props.title: Build on Astro, don't just fork it
props.subtitle: Pages are data. Widgets are a registry. Themes are tokens. This demo is powered entirely by JSON content and the Parche integration.

props.title: Philosophy:
props.description: Simplicity, best practices and high performance.

props.title: What Parche gives you
props.subtitle: A small, coherent core you build on.

items.title: Pages as data
items.description: Author pages as JSON/MD sections, rendered by DynamicRenderer.

items.title: Primitives + widgets
items.description: Foundational primitives consumed via parche:primitives/*, widgets via parche:widgets/*.

items.title: Pluggable apps
items.description: Drop in @parche/blog for routes, collections and RSS.

items.title: OKLCH theming
items.description: A token system that reskins every widget by swapping variables.

items.title: SSR or static
items.description: Runs on any adapter Astro supports. This demo uses the Node adapter.

items.title: SEO built in
items.description: Metadata, Open Graph, JSON-LD and sitemaps out of the box.

props.title: One engine, many outputs
props.content: Parche is the framework; AstroWind is its reference materialization. The same engine drives local pages, blog posts and, later, niche themes.

items.title: Virtual-module registry
items.description: Widgets and primitives resolve through parche:* modules.

items.title: Content-driven
items.description: Swap content sources without touching components.

items.title: Composable
items.description: Add apps and widgets as your site grows.
